To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Coulomb-break-up reactions of the two-neutrons-halo nuclei can be well described within the framework of the adiabatic theory, which uses the realistic three-body ground-state wave function of the halo nucleus.
we have extended the framework of the postform distorted-wave approximation to the description of the Coulomb-induced breakup of the two-nucleon halo nucleus.

(1) the two-body 4He–neutron correlation is the dominant one, (2) the two-body neutron–neutron correlation plays a significant role, (3) the pure Coulomb-breakup theory can account for the bulk of the experimental data taken at below-grazing angles, and (4) the nuclear breakup has a significant influence on the breakup cross section.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the Coulomb-induced breakup of 6 He in the framework of a microscopic three-body model.
the study of the Coulomb dissociation of the halo nucleus 6 He in the energy range from 0.8 MeV to 1.2 MeV per nucleon.
the development of a realistic model for the description of breakup of halo nuclei, and with the application of the model for the description and interpretation of the breakup of 6 He.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Coulomb-break-up data on 6 He are not yet conclusive and more data are needed.
the pure Coulob breakup is not a good theory for the description of Coulomb breakup of two-neutron-halos.
the data can be explained by the pure Coulomb break-up, but the nuclear break-up effects are also present.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the finite-range post-form distorted-wave Born approximation model can describe all the available experimental data for the Coulomb breakup reaction of 6 He.
the two-body 4He–neutron correlation is the most important one for the description of 6He Coulomb breakup.
the finite-range post-form distorted-wave Born approximation is a reliable theory for the description of Coulomb breakup of one- and two-neutron-halos.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two-body correlations in 6 He are not very important for the description of its Coulomb breakup.
the two-neutron halo of 6 He can be described as the two-neutron system weakly bound by the core, which in turn is weakly bound by two neutrons.
the two-body 4He–neutron and the two-body neutron–neutron correlation functions can be used to extract the two-neutron separation energy of 6He from the data of the Coulomb breakups.
